requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the bundled skill meets `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill`. The one weak point is that no test checks the skill's content, and I judge that absence acceptable (see Tests).

**Implementation.** The only `{impl}` site is the `:impl:` anchor in `md/requirements/cli.md` pointing at `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`. It is a prose skill, so I checked each obligation against its text:
- **Bundling.** The skill sits under `assets/skills`. `Cargo.toml` registers that directory as Symposium skills (`package.metadata.symposium.skills`, `source.path = "assets/skills"`). `md/getting_started.md` tells users to use the `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` skill.
- **Read the code and tests.** The opening paragraph tells agents to read the requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation and tests. It also says to follow behavior through the code rather than rely on test names or top-level dispatch.
- **Map every first-party test.** The first inventory covers every runnable test or case, including integration tests, doctests and parameterized cases. A later paragraph requires at least one `{test}` reference with a full requirement or example name on each test definition or case. File-level tags may not stand in for unrelated tests.
- **Map every source unit implementing end-user-visible behavior.** The second inventory lists every explicit function or method in first-party Rust. It also lists public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors and distinct observable branches. Each must carry an `{impl}`, `{test}` or `{cite}` reference. The skill states that a tagged entry point does not cover deeper code and that there is no waiver for uncited functions. It also requires that every end-user-observable result and branch be reviewed against a requirement, and that unclear user-facing candidates stay on a gap list.
- **Report gaps and require independent review.** The skill says to have both inventories independently reviewed against the source and tests before claiming complete coverage. It also says to report mapped counts over total counts, claim 100% only when nothing is unmapped, and list remaining gaps with locations and reasons.

**Extra behavior.** The skill also covers user agreement on inferred requirements, internal-detail requirements, and running `habeas author --all`. The requirement does not specify these, but other requirements do, and they also anchor this skill as `{impl}`. Those are `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill`, `requirements.cli.behavior_review_guidance`, `requirements.cli.internal_detail_guidance` and `requirements.authoring.batch`. So I found no unspecified behavior.

**Marking completeness.** The `Cargo.toml` skills registration is marked `{impl}` for `requirements.integration.symposium_cli`, not for this requirement. It is generic plumbing for all skills, and the skill file itself is the artifact this requirement describes. I do not count that as a gap.

**Tests.** No `{test}` reference exists for this requirement. The deliverable is natural-language guidance, and whether an agent follows it cannot be tested deterministically. Bundling and installation are exercised indirectly by `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py`, which iterates every skill directory under `assets/skills` and checks that Symposium installs it byte-for-byte. That test is tagged `requirements.integration.symposium`. A phrase-presence test on the skill text would add little, so I accept the absence of tests as justified. A grep-style content test would be a possible improvement.
